svg.title: Where Balaam looked down: the plains of Moab
svg.desc: Relief map of the plains of Moab at the north end of the Dead Sea, drawn from SRTM elevation: the Jordan Valley floor below sea level in pale tints, the escarpment and the Moab plateau in deepening browns, with contours at sea level, 400 and 800 metres. Israel's camp is a dashed gold band along the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim (Numbers 33:49), with Shittim at Tall el-Hammam. Three numbered high places on the plateau edge to the south-east are the viewpoints Balak used: 1 Bamoth-baal (dashed as approximate), 2 Pisgah on Mount Nebo and 3 Peor at Khirbet Ayun Musa, each with a red sight line to the camp labelled with what Balaam saw: the outskirts (Numbers 22:41), not all of them (Numbers 23:13), and Israel encamped tribe by tribe (Numbers 24:2), set out in a card below the map. Jericho, Gilgal (dashed) and Heshbon are marked, and a dashed line marks the Roman road from Heshbon past Peor down to the plain, which Joel Kramer suggests the Magi used. An inset shows the wider region: the Arnon, Moab's border where Balak met Balaam (Numbers 22:36), Tell Deir Alla where the Balaam inscription was found, Jerusalem, and an arrow to Pethor by the Euphrates, about 580 km to the north (Numbers 22:5), its site disputed. Two cards separate what the text states from Kramer's identifications, which the study holds. The plate closes with Numbers 24:5.
svg.text: The plains of Moab, Numbers 22:1-25:1, on Joel Kramer's identifications
Peor is the ridge north of Pisgah
The viewpoints run south to north,
the view widening as they near
The Magi may have come by Peor
“How lovely are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel!”
Relief: SRTM 90 m (NASA) via OpenTopoData. Water: Natural Earth. Sites: OpenBible.info,
as Joel Kramer (Expedition Bible) identifies them.
After the manner of Clarence Larkin · the-way.lewy.au
